institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to learn better French and attend a university which was more innoative and different from what I knew at home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, they had a good and informative webside.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of oppertunities to get to know the campus through guided tours. They also had a welcome meeting for all starting their masters with info about the institution. However, unless you paid 250 euro for the introduction week, there was no social planned activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: First I lived in the Cite Universitaire and later I moved to the city center. I found my housing through a facebook group for Danes in Paris.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Socially I found most of my friends through the Cite Universitarie and the Danish Church, when living in the city it is difficult to find connections unless you are very pro-active.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Quite easy, however, some parts of their webside is often not translated to English.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was easy to get into contact with help services at Sciences Po, however, their answering time varried.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As an exchange student you get last pick at choosing classes. This means that you for certain will not get all the classes you prefer. Popular classes were already filled when we got to elect our classes. I had a lot of classes very late in the evening and early in the morning as result of this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared and organized when doing the class registration process. Have a plan A, B, C etc. There are also different class variants and restrictions on what kinds of classes you can choose. Do proper research beforehand. From the time registration opens there is no time to wonder as it only takes a few minutes before all classes are full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware that you will spend a lot of time doing the semester compared to at home, but the exam period is therefore also shorter.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the academic level was lower than in Denmark. You almost never had to analyse anything, just being able to account for concepts. However, you had to spent a lot of time anyways, since a lot of the exams relied on memorization.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was also a lot of group work with groups that you either did not get to choose or was made on the first day of class almost by random just by the people you sat next to. I was in four different groups for various projects and classes. For me it was challanging because people came from very different backgrounds and had very different ideas and academic levels. Plus everyone had different classes/scheldules which made it very difficult to find time to meet. Some people were very unengaged.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
DEMOCRACY IN EUROPE - BACKSLIDING AND COMPETITION IN MULTI-LEVEL SYSTEMS (202510 - 17737)
SECURITIZATION AT WORK: CASE STUDIES ACROSS SECTORS (202510 - 17267)
DEEP-TIME POLITICS: INTERGENERATIONAL AND PLANETARY RESPONSIBILITIES (202510 - 19142)
CLIMATE CHANGE AND SECURITY, A GEOPOLITICAL AND MULTISCALE PERSPECTIVE (202510 - 18378)
GENDER AND THE LAW: CONVERGENCES AND DIVERGENCES IN LATIN AMERICA (202510 - 19032)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Gender and the law had a professor that was very inspiring and engaging. I was surprised at how much I enjoyed it and the work amount was very sufficient.
Climate Change and Security had likewise a very good professor and was super interesting. However, becuase she works during the day the class is every semester in the evening, for me it was from 19.15-21-15.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different activities were offered.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do a language course in French. Engage in Fredags Bar in Frederikskirken.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I did not have a lot of time to big excursions. If you are planning on this, do it in september as the academic pressure gets more intense later.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in the social clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: French academics are not as structured as we are used to in Denmark which can be frustrating.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Eating out for cheaper.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to use a lot of time on academics.
Choose classes carefully.
You cannot miss anymore than two classes per class.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Grades are based more on class participation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Paris is a very dynamic city with a lot of things to do.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having as much freetime as expected.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
